fault_tolerant_sources.title: Fast Black-Box Quantum State Preparation
roles: geometric precision-index state and individual-bit oracle
capped geometric source and its preparation lineage
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The explicit exact preparation uses a linear-size unary temporary, binary conversion, and routing cleanup. Logarithmic source-register width is not a logarithmic peak-clean-workspace guarantee. No strict gate-count improvement over the routing variants is asserted.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Trading T gates for dirty qubits in state preparation and unitary synthesis
roles: exact dirty-assisted lookup and complete dirty-bank restoration
finite-width Clifford+T circuit counting
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Dirty lookup banks do not replace the initialized output program. The basis-state cancellation identity extends to reference-entangled inputs by linearity. Neither dirty lookup nor the counting method is claimed as new.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Quantum state preparation with optimal T-count
roles: optimal unrestricted state-preparation and diagonal-synthesis benchmarks
ancilla-independent diagonal lower bound used through a frame subfamily
Boolean and single-qubit synthesis primitives
complete multiplexors and geometric layer-error allocation
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: A generic preparation theorem does not prescribe the remaining frame columns. An unrestricted-ancilla result does not supply the clean/dirty tradeoff. Multiplexor synthesis and geometric error allocation are already in Appendix B.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Unitary Synthesis with Fewer T Gates
roles: general-unitary comparison
batching controlled single-qubit instruction tables
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Use the published precision-dependent T and ancilla bounds separately. The displayed instruction-word construction uses initialized program registers and does not directly give the stated small-clean/dirty frame theorem.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Optimal T Counts under Sparsity: from QROM to State Preparation and Block Encoding
roles: sparse QROM and sparse-state comparison
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Different input families; no generic full-frame or bounded-clean-workspace theorem is imported.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Hamiltonian Simulation in the Interaction Picture
roles: coherent product compression with logarithmic failure-history work
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The compression gadget and history counter are inherited mechanisms; the local contribution is their integration with residual factorization and a shared precision source.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Time-marching based quantum solvers for time-dependent linear differential equations
roles: simplified coherent compression gadget and reusable block workspace
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Reusing initialized block work with a logarithmic counter is established prior art. It does not replace the queried block encoding's peak initialized-work requirement with dirty work.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Methods for Reducing Ancilla-Overhead in Block Encodings
roles: ancilla-uncomputation comparison
restricted exact-history ancilla lower bound
approximate product compression comparison
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The uncomputation procedure still queries the original block encoding with its initialized work. Exact-product lower bounds concern the defined MCM circuit class, not unrestricted Hopf compilation. Approximate compression needs near-identity full dilations, not only near-identity accepted blocks.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Multi-qubit controlled gate with optimal T-count
roles: leading precision constants for complete multiplexed SU(2) synthesis
explicit precision-length clean program with dirty lookup
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The displayed dirty-assisted circuit uses 3L+O(n)+o(L) clean qubits under a typical-target guarantee. Its ancilla-free alternative has order NL+Nn cost. The comparison uses channel distance and does not imply a literal-phase two-clean compiler for every target.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Quantum Circuits for General Unitaries: Improved T-Count via Block Flattening and Dilation
roles: current generic-unitary upper-bound comparison
complete initialized-isometry error convention
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: For N=2^n and n+L<=N, the theorem gives O(n N^(5/4)(n+L)^(5/8)) T gates with O(N sqrt(n+L)) clean ancillas. It treats arbitrary unitaries, not the prescribed small-clean/dirty frame budget. Tan must not be described as the newest generic upper bound.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Unitary Synthesis with Near-Optimal T-Count for Near-Clifford Unitaries
roles: instance-dependent synthesis in phase-optimized Frobenius distance to the Clifford group
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Uses initialized ancillas with a detailed diamond-distance conclusion. Does not supply the literal-phase two-clean guarantee or the structured frame's worst-case frontier.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Halving the cost of QROM
roles: improved dirty-QROM constants and bit-packet scheduling context
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The displayed construction retains an initialized output word. Its improvements preserve the asymptotic lookup tradeoff used here; no constant-factor superiority is claimed.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: Optimal T-Count for Block Encodings of Fermionic and Spin Hamiltonians
roles: recent clean-ancilla compression for block-encoding lower bounds
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: Compresses to at most n+2T clean ancillas and can change normalization. It is not a two-clean unitary implementation result or a lower bound for the Hopf endpoint.

fault_tolerant_sources.title: An algorithm for the T-count
roles: Pauli-transfer representation and square-root-of-two denominator lower-bound method
fault_tolerant_sources.boundary: The local proof specializes the method to the geometric operator source and explicitly extends the scalar witness through returned clean and dirty helpers. It is not an additive full-frame lower bound.

fault_tolerant_claim_policy.audit_scope: Primary-source comparison through 2026-09-22, including current generic-unitary and controlled-gate bounds, dirty-QROM refinements, and block-product compression; bounded technical comparison, not certification of priority
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.model: Coherent Clifford+T compilation with a literal-phase complete initialized-isometry error bound over arbitrary logical, dirty and reference inputs. The sufficient-clean frame compiler returns dirty work exactly; the two-clean operator-source compiler includes approximate dirty-core return in the norm and returns lookup work exactly. Budgets, precision and Clifford cost are separate.
do_not_claim: invention of optimal unrestricted state preparation or diagonal synthesis
invention of multiplexor synthesis or geometric layer-error allocation
invention of geometric precision indexing or dyadic bit-oracle sampling
invention of dirty lookup, selector cancellation, or borrowed-bit echoes
invention of logarithmic failure-history storage, block-product compression, Clifford-algebra loaders, or oblivious amplification
a two-clean unitary compiler inferred from a block-ancilla uncomputation theorem
new finite-width counting or ancilla-independent lower-bound machinery
one circuit simultaneously optimal in CNOT size, depth, and T count
a general constant-clean-workspace frame lower bound from a small-source obstruction
differentiation of the compiled circuit family or optimal gradient-query complexity
priority inferred from absence of a matching result in a bounded search
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.compact_source_role: An explicit exact O(L)-T, O(log L)-peak-clean implementation of the established capped geometric source, with ordinary binary labels and exact temporary return.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.direct_sampler_role: A complete addressed SU(2) compiler using fixed Pauli atoms, geometric bit sampling, charged lookup, and standard oblivious amplitude amplification. Its direct frame composition already yields the matching count in polynomial-precision examples.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.principal_contribution: The full-frame precision/workspace upper construction combines residual grouping and a shared accepted-branch shift source with inherited failure compression and amplification. A distinct geometric operator source gives the two-clean frame construction and the matching two-clean literal-diagonal frontier. Imported lower bounds match only the stated regimes.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.all_clean_budget_corollary: A splice of supported compilers under an additional workspace/precision condition; not a new independent lower bound.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.moderate_precision_boundary: The L=n^2, a=Theta(n), b=Theta(n sqrt(N)) witness is already attained by the earlier direct sampler and must not be presented as an incremental checkpoint-28 gain.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.qbp_bridge: At fixed parameters, complete-isometry and observable-implementation error bound the bias of a bounded-score estimator. No derivative of the classically selected Clifford+T word is taken.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.evidence_boundary: Analytic construction and finite component checks; no general emitted fault-tolerant frame compiler is claimed.
fault_tolerant_claim_policy.review_status: Internal source and proof audit; broader independent review remains necessary before submission.
